claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3, with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=3+2/m, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, all sufficiently large integers are sums of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 3, with m=min D, gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>=3+2/m, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, all sufficiently large integers are sums of finitely many remaining occurrences d^j, each pair (d,j) used at most once; coincident numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.
quadruple.stage: Finite sets of integer bases, countable locally finite labelled power occurrences, exact rational reciprocal mass, and finite subset sums in the integers.

shape.objects: Inputs are arbitrary finite D, positive k and finite occurrence deletions F; outputs are finite occurrence subsets for each sufficiently large n. Finite base partitions are built by adjoining unused bases, and disjoint finite subsets of occurrence supplies combine by union. All underlying integers, rational sums, finite sets, pairs and functions have core Lean or Mathlib definitions; no custom foundational object is required. Finite selections can be random variables, but no spread estimate is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such finite D, every positive integer k and every finite labelled deletion F, there exists N(D,k,F), for every integer n>=N there is a finite subset of the remaining labels whose values sum to n. The leading quantifiers are universal over countably encoded inputs; the existential statement is covering, not full measure.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-coverage assertion at the exact stated reciprocal threshold. It is not an optimization problem for that threshold. An unspecified finite N(D,k,F) settles the claim; no explicit quantitative bound on N is requested.
shape.ambient_structure: Order and divisibility coexist with labelled finite-set union and addition. Combining disjoint occurrence supports adds their sums, permitting a finite interval to amplify against a bounded-gap remainder. Exact per-base geometric sums and finite cyclic residue groups retain the pure-power structure. No random-event dependence estimate or density-increment piece system is supplied.
shape.symmetries: Permuting labels within equal numerical values preserves availability; arbitrary numerical deduplication does not. Disjoint-support union is the additive operation. Translation or dilation of D does not preserve the hypotheses, and no closed density-increment system is asserted.
shape.configuration: Every sufficiently large n must be a positive sum using each allowed pair (d,j) at most once. Finite prefixes need not be complete, and arbitrary restriction to a base subfamily can destroy both reciprocal mass and gcd one. Any finite-correction amplification must keep its correction labels disjoint from the reserved bounded-gap supply.
shape.extremal_candidate: No optimal reciprocal threshold or minimum certificate is claimed. The candidate is a feasible three-way partition, with the accepted minimum-preserving gcd-one core placed in the correction component.
shape.finite_certificates: For fixed D,k,F a finite interval of length at least a rigorously bounded gap constant, represented on labels disjoint from the infinite gap-bounded reserve, is a sufficient finite seed. Its smallest length within this amplification is determined by that gap bound. Its universal existence and the labelled version of the cited criterion are not yet proved in this attack. No finite root domain or complete all-D computation is supplied.
shape.monotonicity: Representability is preserved by adding unused allowed labels; increasing k or deleting more labels can only remove representations. The claim includes every positive k, beginning with k=1, but no fixed k or finite prefix decides all k. The high/low mass route leaves the complementary mass range explicitly open.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All finite D, arbitrarily large minimum and cardinality, every positive cutoff k and every finite deletion F. The representation threshold may depend on all three inputs.
shape.proof_shape: Completed local analytical candidate: occurrence-indexed bounded gaps, disjoint interval/reserve amplification, finite-correction compact-group proof using the published piecewise-Bohr sumset theorem, the accepted reciprocal core, and a strict first-crossing partition. All cutoffs, finite deletions, and the inclusive mass endpoint are covered. A dovetailed finite-seed and representation search has proved termination; no mathematical program was run.
shape.neighbours: Known true for numerical sets: Fan's three-component completeness criterion, arXiv:2607.14071v3 Corollary2.3. Known true locally: minimum-preserving reciprocal-core selection, checkpoint-000008 and acceptance-000001. Known false: the generic strong-profile and signed-profile seed inferences, acceptances000003 and000004; those are not pure-power counterexamples. The root and complementary low-mass range remain open. Finite base partitions and finite support configurations are checkable neighbours. No proved property-reflecting category correspondence or verbatim simpler model is recorded.
shape.known_bounds: Accepted core bound is 1<=sigma(E)<1+1/minD with minD retained. Published Bergelson-Simmons Theorem1.23 uses three bounded-deficit components plus a separate gcd correction component; Fan reduces the numerical-set engine to three components. Previous proxy counterexamples and a fourth-moment obstruction show why abstract arithmetic profiles and an ordinary Gaussian approximation do not supply the pure-power seed. No completed proof, counterexample compression, optimal threshold, first-moment success estimate, uniform finite reduction, or exhaustive computational range is recorded for this new claim.
shape.missing_input: No missing lemma remains in the local candidate proof at moves/001-high-mass-completeness.md. Independent checkpoint/result review and acceptance are still required. The original complementary mass range remains open outside this admitted claim.
shape.base_theory: Classical arithmetic, real analysis and compact-group arguments in ZFC with choice. No additional axiom, forcing principle, guessing principle or uncountable independence hypothesis is used. These objects and any finite rational or residue checks lie within Lean's standard classical axioms, but no formal verification or mathematical computation is admitted.
